title: Longest subarray with given sum K(positives)
stepTitle: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
category: Solve Problems on Arrays [Easy -> Medium -> Hard]
problemStatement: Longest subarray with sum exactly K, where all elements are positive.
intuition: With strictly positive numbers, extending the window only grows the sum and shrinking only reduces it — that monotonicity is what makes a two-pointer window valid.

approaches.title: Brute: all subarrays
approaches.idea: Fix the start, extend the end, track sums.

approaches.title: Optimal: two-pointer window
approaches.idea: Grow right; while sum > k shrink from the left; record when sum == k.
approaches.time: O(n) — each index enters and leaves once
approaches.whyWorks: Positivity makes window sum monotonic in both pointers, so no valid window is skipped.

commonMistakes: Reusing this window when zeros or negatives are allowed — it silently breaks
patternRecognition: Positive weights + target sum -> sliding window; otherwise prefix-sum hashing
followUps: Same problem with negatives (#52 — prefix sums + hash map)
Count subarrays with sum K instead of the longest
interviewInsight: State the positivity precondition explicitly — interviewers deliberately follow up with negatives.
